requirements.heading: Introduction
requirements.text: This MAY be used in conjunction with the CHUNKING [RFC3030] mechanism so that chunks of the message can come from an external IMAP server.

requirements.heading: SMTP Submission Extension Registration
requirements.text: This extends the Message Submission protocol on port 587 and MUST NOT be advertised by a regular SMTP [RFC2821] server on port 25 that acts as a relay for incoming mail from other SMTP relays.

requirements.heading: SMTP Submission Extension Registration
requirements.text: The only argument defined at this time is the "imap" argument, which MUST be present in order to use IMAP URLs with BURL.

requirements.heading: SMTP Submission Extension Registration
requirements.text: Clients MUST ignore other arguments after the BURL EHLO keyword unless they are defined by a subsequent IETF standards track specification.

requirements.heading: BURL Transaction
requirements.text: If PIPELINING [RFC2920] is advertised, the client MAY send the entire transaction in one round trip.

requirements.heading: BURL Transaction
requirements.text: A more sophisticated BURL transaction MAY occur when the server also advertises CHUNKING [RFC3030].

requirements.heading: BURL Transaction
requirements.text: However, it MUST wait for the results of the "LAST" BDAT or BURL command prior to initiating a new transaction.

requirements.heading: The BURL IMAP Options
requirements.text: Subsequent to a successful SMTP AUTH command, the submission server MAY indicate a prearranged trust relationship with a specific IMAP server by including a BURL EHLO keyword argument of the form "imap://imap.example.com".

requirements.heading: The BURL IMAP Options
requirements.text: The authentication identity and password used for submit credentials MUST be configurable.

requirements.heading: The BURL IMAP Options
requirements.text: If the IMAP URL uses the "submit+" access identifier prefix, the submit server MUST refuse the BURL command unless the userid in the URL's <access> token matches the submit client's authorization identity.

requirements.heading: The BURL IMAP Options
requirements.text: server SHOULD forward the client's credentials if and only if the submit server knows that the IMAP server is in the same administrative domain.

requirements.heading: The BURL IMAP Options
requirements.text: If the submit server supports SASL mechanisms other than PLAIN, it MUST implement a configuration in which the submit server's embedded IMAP client uses STARTTLS and SASL PLAIN with the submit server's authentication identity and password (for the respective IMAP server) and the submit client's authorization identity.

requirements.heading: Formal Syntax
requirements.text: A submit server that advertises BURL MUST also advertise 8BITMIME [RFC1652] and perform the down conversion described in that specification on the resulting complete message if 8-bit data is received with the BURL command and passed to a 7-bit server.

requirements.heading: Formal Syntax
requirements.text: If the URL argument to BURL refers to binary data, then the submit server MAY refuse the command or down convert as described in Binary SMTP [RFC3030].

requirements.heading: Formal Syntax
requirements.text: The Submit server MAY refuse to accept a BURL command or combination of BURL and BDAT commands that result in un-encoded 8-bit data in mail or MIME [RFC2045] headers.

requirements.heading: Formal Syntax
requirements.text: Alternatively, the server MAY accept such data and down convert to MIME header encoding [RFC2047].

requirements.heading: Response Codes
requirements.text: This list is not exhaustive, and BURL clients MUST tolerate any valid SMTP response code.

requirements.heading: Security Considerations
requirements.text: To address this expectation, the message submission server SHOULD use STARTTLS or a mechanism providing equivalent data confidentiality when fetching the content referenced by that URL.
